dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: Huh? Were you talking to me? Sorry, I didn't see you there. Are you here to accept the commission regarding "Tales of Humanity"?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's my reputation at the Court of Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: If you can help solve our readers' troubles, I'm sure they'd be willing to compensate you for your efforts.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: What nice weather today — doesn't it just put you in the mood to help some people in need?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's my reputation at the Court of Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: "A kind soul who always knows what to do..." Everyone's got a rather positive opinion of you, I must say.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: Well met, dear. Your fine deeds are well-known amongst our readers — indeed, we've received a good number of thank-you letters.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: Are you here to take up a commission again? Hehe, what a noble soul you are.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's my reputation at the Court of Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: I and all our readers are thankful for your contributions. If you should need any help in the future, just let me know — we, too, hope that we'll be able to do something for you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about "Tales of Humanity"...

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: One of the primary reasons we had for establishing our newspaper was to ensure that information flows and that everyone can understand what's happening around them.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: Slowly, we moved to not only attempting to let readers "know," but to also let them "express" themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: Thus, "Tales of Humanity" was born. Everyone can write in to this column, and similarly, everyone can read it.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: As for the result... Well, you've seen it, haven't you? Our prints are practically drowning in all manner of content.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: But that's not a bad thing. In my experience, listeners also need some light reading to go with their explosive news.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: Additionally, being able to help our readers does our reputation good.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: In other words, we'll be troubling you somewhat further. Fret not — you will find our payment quite suitable.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: See you. Have a lovely day.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you tell me about Charlotte?

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: Sure! She's one of our journalists... Is she in trouble again?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not really.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: Well, that's good. She is a live correspondent, and they tend to put themselves in the line of fire — I almost thought that someone had come to make a threat again.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: Ah, don't worry, we have our ways of dealing with such matters.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: After all, we'd have gone bust a long time ago if we couldn't handle ourselves in a little tussle or two.
